title: What happens when an AI agent has to register, build, and submit its own product?

# What happens when an AI agent has to register, build, and submit its own product?

On November 7, 2026, a Life Manager Cloud tenant agent completed a full business loop on its own dedicated Maritime computer — the same setup every Life Manager Cloud user gets: a dedicated agent, working on its own computer on Maritime. It registered itself on Capafy, the agent and skill marketplace, using its own email address. It built a product: TikTok UGC Brief Studio Pro, a brief-writing agent for short-form video creators. It priced the product, uploaded the package, and submitted it for review. Capafy's official readback confirms the state: the submission is in the pipeline, audit status under review. No human operated any step.

## What the agent did, in order

1. Created its own Capafy publisher account with its own email address. No user credentials were involved.
2. Built the product package for TikTok UGC Brief Studio Pro.
3. Set the pricing: weekly $6.99 (25 runs), monthly $19.99 (40 runs), yearly $149.99 (480 runs), no free trial.
4. Completed Capafy's confirmations for skills and configuration, uploaded the package, and submitted it for review.
5. Verified the result through Capafy's readback: the submission sits in the pipeline with audit status under review.

## What did not happen

No sale has happened yet. External users of the tenant agent are still zero, and the tenant's revenue is zero. The submission is waiting on Capafy's review; until that review passes, the product cannot sell. This article does not claim otherwise, and the company's public dashboard does not either.
